pages.title: Read and answer
pages.instruction: Listen and read Ana’s update. Listen to Ana first, then read her update and answer the questions
pages.subject: A busy week at home
paragraphs: Kim has just come back from visiting her family in Korea. Tomorrow, she’s coming over for coffee. I’ve been painting my flat all week, so I have a lot to show her. I’ve finished the living room and the kitchen, but I haven’t started the bedroom yet.

I’ve also been running every morning for two weeks. Getting up early was hard at first, but now I enjoy it. In the evenings, I’ve been baking. I’ve made three cakes this week, and I’m saving a slice for Kim.
It’s been a productive week, but I haven’t had much time for myself. This weekend, I want to take a break from painting and catch up with my friend.

titleAudio.text:
Kim has just come back from visiting her family in Korea. Tomorrow, she’s coming over for coffee. I’ve been painting my flat all week, so I have a lot to show her. I’ve finished the living room and the kitchen, but I haven’t started the bedroom yet.

I’ve also been running every morning for two weeks. Getting up early was hard at first, but now I enjoy it. In the evenings, I’ve been baking. I’ve made three cakes this week, and I’m saving a slice for Kim.

It’s been a productive week, but I haven’t had much time for myself. This weekend, I want to take a break from painting and catch up with my friend.

questions.prompt: Which rooms has Ana finished, and which one is next?
questions.hint: Two rooms are finished; one room is still waiting
questions.answer: She has finished the living room and the kitchen. The bedroom is next.

questions.prompt: How often does Ana run, and how long has she been doing it?
questions.hint: Look for a daily habit and a period of time
questions.answer: She has been running every morning for two weeks.

questions.prompt: Why does Ana want to take a break this weekend?
questions.hint: Think about her busy week and the time she has had for herself
questions.answer: She has been busy painting, running and baking, and she has not had much time for herself. She wants to catch up with Kim.

pages.title: Catch up on your week
pages.instruction: Compare your week with your teacher’s. Ask about something they have been doing

items.prompt: What have you been busy with this week?
items.cue: Tell me about work, study or something you do at home, then ask me
items.hint: I’ve been cooking more this week. What have you been doing?

items.prompt: Have you finished anything, or are you still working on it?
items.cue: Give me one result or tell me what you still need to do
items.hint: I haven’t finished my book yet. I’ve still got two chapters to read

items.prompt: Have you had the kind of week you wanted?
items.cue: Say what you would keep or change. Ask about one thing I mentioned
items.hint: I’d like more time to read. How did you find time for your hobby?

pages.title: Compare present perfect simple and continuous
pages.instruction: Use the continuous form to focus on activity and the simple form to focus on a result or amount

rows.subject: Ask about the focus
rows.verb: How long have you been + -ing? / How many have you + participle?
rows.example: How long have you been painting? How many rooms have you painted?

pages.note: A simple form can also describe a continuing situation: I’ve known her for years. The continuous form does not itself tell us whether the activity has just stopped or continues.

pages.title: Role-play the situation
pages.instruction: Catch up with a friend. Choose a topic, share recent activities and ask about mine

pages.title: Listen and answer
pages.instruction: A message from Leo. Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana! It’s Leo. We’ve finished the invitations for the party, so that’s one thing off the list. We’ve also seen eleven possible places now, but we haven’t chosen one yet. We’ve been visiting places every weekend for three weeks, and it’s taking longer than I expected. Carla wants space for dancing, while I’d be happy with a barbecue in the park. Could you help us think about what matters most before we book another visit? The invitations are ready, but the venue decision is still open
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana! It’s Leo. We’ve finished the invitations for the party, so that’s one thing off the list. We’ve also seen eleven possible places now, but we haven’t chosen one yet. We’ve been visiting places every weekend for three weeks, and it’s taking longer than I expected. Carla wants space for dancing, while I’d be happy with a barbecue in the park. Could you help us think about what matters most before we book another visit? The invitations are ready, but the venue decision is still open.
